hook: The king of Spain at its height, who sent the Armada against England.

pages.x: Philip was born in Valladolid in 1527, the son of the emperor Charles V. In 1556 his father handed him Spain, the Netherlands, much of Italy and the Americas.

pages.t: King of England, for a while
pages.x: In 1554 he married Queen Mary I of England, eleven years older than him, and was king of England while she lived. They had no children. When Mary died in 1558 he proposed to her sister Elizabeth, who turned him down.

He built El Escorial, a vast granite palace, monastery and royal tomb near Madrid. From a small room there, with a window onto the high altar, he ruled his empire by paperwork, reading and scribbling notes on thousands of documents.

In 1571 a fleet of Spain, Venice and the pope, led by his half-brother Don John of Austria, smashed the Ottoman navy at Lepanto, off Greece, the largest sea battle in centuries. A young soldier called Cervantes was wounded there.
In 1580 he took the throne of Portugal as well, joining the two greatest overseas empires. The Philippines had already been named after him.

His harsh rule and persecution of Protestants set off the Dutch Revolt, an 80-year war. In 1588 he sent the Spanish Armada of 130 ships against England. It was beaten off, then wrecked by storms on the way home.
Despite all the silver of the Americas, his wars bankrupted Spain four times. He died in 1598 at El Escorial, after a long and painful illness.
Philip II ruled Spain at its peak, the champion of Catholic Europe against Protestants and Ottomans. His failures in the Netherlands and against England marked the start of Spain's slow decline.
pts: Ruled Spain at the height of its power
Gave his name to the Philippines
